A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from SAVCD to Self-Aug. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments across four LVLMs, alongside ablations, latency measurements and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds Qwen3-VL benchmark results, an operational-knowledge ablation and a failure analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, query-conditioned augmentation selection, the six augmentations, SAT thresholding and contrastive sampling are unchanged. Appendix B's prompts also match. Renaming SAVCD to Self-Aug and testing additional ablated configurations do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate POPE-MSCOCO, POPE-AOKVQA, MME-P, MMVP, LLaVA-Bench, MM-Vet and MMHal-Bench. The added model evaluations use retained tasks and datasets. Video remains a proposed future direction in both versions.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparators remain multinomial sampling, VCD and VACoDe. Table 6 newly includes the baseline within the prompt-ablation comparison, while new Table 7 compares standalone expert and amateur sampling against contrasted sampling. These are limited additions to comparison controls.

E3.justification: V2 extends the existing evaluation protocol to Qwen3-VL-8B and adds a Qwen3-VL-32B expert/amateur/contrast comparison. The prompt ablation adds a condition removing operational definitions. Existing metrics, augmentation parameters and default decoding hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds an all-components-off condition, testing operational knowledge against the existing reasoning/ICL-off configuration. Table 7 adds a failure analysis on MMVP and MME-P using Qwen3-VL-32B. Existing SAT sensitivity studies, augmentation comparisons and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations from five main-experiment runs and three ablation runs with different seeds. The new failure analysis also uses three runs and the same uncertainty reporting practice; no new statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: V2 substantially expands results with Qwen3-VL-8B evaluations across all seven benchmarks, including Self-Aug MMVP accuracy of 60.50 ± 0.64. Table 6 adds 1312.39 ± 11.71 for the all-components-off condition. Table 7 adds failure findings: Qwen3-VL-32B obtains MME-P 1789.94 ± 0.73 with contrasted sampling versus 1798.15 ± 8.64 with expert-only sampling. Corresponding original results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5 adds explicit logit-ordering assumptions for false and true positives and derives suppression of a false-positive logit when its amateur logit exceeds its expert logit. This is a limited mathematical failure argument; the original method equations remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain training-free, query-aware augmentation selection and entropy-aware truncation to improve factual consistency. Updating the abstract and introduction from four to five evaluated LVLMs describes additional validation rather than a substantively different core claim.

C2.justification: V2 identifies operational knowledge as the main contributor in the prompt ablation and adds a limitation concerning insufficient expert/amateur separation. Section 3.2 changes APC's low-confidence failure explanation from retaining implausible tokens to discarding correct tokens. The detailed video-extension proposals in Appendix F are condensed into the discussion.

D1.justification: The project-page address is updated, and Appendix C adds a description of the Qwen3-VL backbone. Existing prompts and augmentation implementation parameters are retained. The GPT-4o-mini and temperature-zero disclosure moves from Appendix A to Section 4.1, so it is not newly supplied information.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bai et al. (2025), listed as the Qwen2.5-VL technical report despite being cited for Qwen3-VL, and removes Huang et al.'s hallucination survey and Ali et al.'s 2023 video-restoration work. VACoDe's description changes from minimizing L2 distance to using it as a selection score. Overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 renames the paper and method, updates the publication header and affiliations, and changes Section 5 into a discussion containing failure cases and limitations. Appendix F is condensed into that discussion, and references are consolidated. Most existing prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain model blocks, Table 6 gains an operational-knowledge column and rows, and a new failure-results Table 7 is added. Table styling and Figure 2 formatting are revised. Existing appendix figures and the oracle table are renumbered and repositioned, retaining their results.

improvement.justification: The new operational-knowledge control and failure study address gaps in v1's evidence about why the method works and when it may fail. Qwen3-VL results broaden validation while preserving the original experiments. These are incremental gains: aggregate scores support the proposed failure mechanism only indirectly, and the new Qwen3-VL citation points to a Qwen2.5-VL report.
